diagnosis.summary: All four services are under a large traffic surge, and payment-service is simultaneously returning 5xx errors on 47.0% of requests with p95 latency at 4.38 s. Order-service reflects both problems, with 23.3% of its requests failing and p95 latency at 4.48 s.
diagnosis.root_cause: A traffic surge across all four services and a concurrent fault in payment-service, active at the same time, are the most likely root cause.
evidence: Request rates surged across every service: product-service rose from 14.98 to 130.0 rps (about 8.7x), cart-service from 2.05 to 29.8 rps (about 14.5x), order-service from 2.97 to 37.9 rps (about 12.8x), and payment-service from 0.94 to 18.75 rps (about 19.9x).
Payment-service p95 latency rose from 4.51 ms to 4384.69 ms, a 973x increase, while its 5xx error rate moved from 0 to 47.0%.
Order-service p95 latency rose from 25.06 ms to 4476.09 ms, about 179x its baseline, and its 5xx error rate moved from 0 to 23.3%.
Order-service recorded 529 dependency errors per minute against payment-service (up from 0), and p95 time spent calling payment-service rose from 22.15 ms to 4881.05 ms, a 220x increase.
recommended_actions: Investigate payment-service Lambda logs and concurrency metrics immediately to identify why 47% of requests are returning 5xx at 4.38 s p95, as this is the highest user-facing error rate and directly affects order-service.
Apply rate and burst limits on the API Gateway stage to cap incoming traffic while both faults are being worked, protecting Lambda concurrency shared across all functions.

Check Lambda throttle counts on all four services, since the account's concurrent execution pool is shared and the surge across product-service, cart-service, order-service and payment-service may be exhausting it.
Once payment-service is stabilised, recheck order-service error rate and dependency error count to confirm improvement before making further changes.
Record the timeline of each signal as observed without linking one fault to the other, so post-incident analysis can distinguish the traffic surge from the payment-service fault.
